architecture.title: Policy as code — where a policy is written, checked, stored and enforced
architecture.caption: You write the YAML on the laptop and check it twice: policykit (the course's teaching model, semantic rules) and the real OpenShell 0.0.111 CLI as an offline parser (structure). On the Spark, the gateway validates and stores each change as a policy revision and pushes it to the sandbox. The network half (proxy + OPA) is hot-reloadable; the filesystem and process half (Landlock, seccomp) is locked at creation. NemoClaw adds presets on top, and the TUI turns an approved denial into a new revision. (Research tutorial Part 2, citing the OpenShell security best practices and sandbox-policies pages.)

sequence.title: The iterate loop: deny → observe → allow → verify
sequence.caption: The agent's first call is denied because no network_policies entry matches. You read the denial in `openshell logs --source sandbox`, preview the fix with `--dry-run` (the gateway merges it into the live policy and sends nothing), then apply it with `--wait`. The gateway stores a new revision and the proxy loads it without restarting the sandbox. The commands are the research tutorial's Lab 2.3; the --dry-run and --wait behaviour was checked against the laptop CLI 0.0.111.

charts.title: Fourteen broken policies — who catches them on the laptop?
charts.caption: Counted from lab 03-2 run on this Mac: policykit caught 12 of 14, the OpenShell 0.0.111 parser caught 7 of 14. The seven policykit-only cases are semantic (root, read_write [/], missing port, access typo, …) — on a Spark the gateway refuses those at push time. The two parser-only cases are rule-shape mistakes policykit does not model.

charts.title: Sixteen --add-endpoint specs — CLI vs policykit
charts.caption: Counted from lab 03-3 step 1 on this Mac. The two 'CLI parses' cases are `::rest` (the research tutorial says the gateway rejects it) and `::sql` (a protocol the 0.0.111 CLI knows and policykit does not). The four 'CLI rejects' cases are checks policykit lacks: mcp in a spec, enforcement without protocol, tcp with an access mode, an unknown option.
